data.text: The evidence is clear. Let me finalize.

data.reason: The firewall's WAN interface vtnet0 has a wedged VirtIO transmit path — repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link DOWN/UP flapping — so traffic cannot leave the firewall even though DHCP reloads succeed; the ARP entry for the ISP gateway 198.51.100.1 is "(incomplete)" and outbound packets fail with ENOBUFS ("No buffer space available").

data.cause: The firewall's WAN interface vtnet0 has a wedged VirtIO transmit path — repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link DOWN/UP flapping — so traffic cannot leave the firewall even though DHCP reloads succeed; the ARP entry for the ISP gateway 198.51.100.1 is "(incomplete)" and outbound packets fail with ENOBUFS ("No buffer space available").
evidence: dmesg -a shows repeated 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' interleaved with 'vtnet0: link state changed to DOWN/UP', indicating the NIC TX queue repeatedly hangs and the link flaps
arp -a -n shows the ISP next hop '198.51.100.1 at (incomplete)' — the gateway MAC never resolves, so no frames reach the provider

ping -c 3 198.51.100.1 and ping -c 3 8.8.8.8 both fail with 'sendto: No buffer space available' (ENOBUFS), 100% loss, while ifconfig shows vtnet0 UP/RUNNING with a valid lease 198.51.100.27 and netstat -rn shows the default route via 198.51.100.1 intact
netstat -i shows 48211 output errors on vtnet0 (Oerrs) versus 0 on the LAN vtnet1, localizing the fault to the WAN NIC

/var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl: 4 WAN reloads during this outage all returned rc=0 yet internet stayed down; at 03:30 the watchdog logged decision action=none reason=reload_cap (reloads_24h=12/12) — DHCP-level reload does not clear the stuck driver

/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl and modem-metrics.jsonl show the cable modem re-registered ('registration complete') and is now OPERATIONAL (min_snr ~37.7), so the provider/modem side recovered and is not what keeps traffic from egressing
data.recommendation: Reboot the firewall (gw.lan) to reset the hung vtnet0 VirtIO driver and its transmit queue. A wan_reload only renews the DHCP lease and has already been tried 4 times this outage without effect (and hit the 12/24h cap), so it will not clear a wedged NIC; a full reboot re-initializes the interface. The maintainer is away, so request the reboot via the harness. After recovery, investigate the vtnet0 driver/host that is producing TX watchdog timeouts, and consider raising the watchdog's reload cap or having it escalate to a host reboot when repeated reloads fail.
data.detail: vtnet0 WAN NIC transmit queue stalls (watchdog timeouts), link flaps, gateway unreachable at L2
